key_insight: Boron redistributes to defects in TiAl alloys, locally pinning dislocations and suppressing deformation twinning to strengthen the material at high temperature.
engineering_relevance: Controlling boron content and defect populations could help design stronger high-temperature TiAl alloys, while accounting for brittle borides and interface-dependent adhesion.
method: Hybrid grand-canonical Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics simulations
Newly developed high-fidelity machine-learning interatomic potential
Atomistic analysis of boron segregation, defect interactions, and deformation
evidence_signal: In simulated polycrystalline TiAl at 900 K, 1 at.% boron increased average flow stress by 9.4% and reduced shear strain accumulation.
watch_item: The strengthening result is simulation-based; experimental validation and assessment across processing conditions are needed before alloy-design deployment.
paper_title: Atomistic insight into defect-mediated boron redistribution and high-temperature strengthening in TiAl alloys
